title: GRIP: In-Parameter Graph Reasoning through Fine-Tuning Large Language Models

problem.claim: Effectively adapting large language models to structural data such as knowledge graphs or web graphs is challenging.

gap.claim: Existing graph-to-text and graph-encoding approaches can incur substantial token or training and alignment costs and may suffer from poor modality alignment.

contributions.claim: GRIP internalizes relational graph knowledge directly into large language model parameters through fine-tuning tasks, without heavy graph serialization or specialized graph encoding modules.
GRIP stores acquired structural knowledge in lightweight LoRA modules for use across multiple tasks over the internalized graph.
The fine-tuned model can perform graph-related tasks without accessing the original graph as inference-time context.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments validate their approach.
For graphs that exceed the LLM context window, the authors report that GRIP consistently outperforms LLM baselines by leveraging internalized graph knowledge.
For small-scale graphs, the authors report comparable performance with substantially lower inference cost.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are capable of modeling sequential text and generalizing across tasks.
Adapting LLMs to structural graph data remains difficult.
Existing approaches use costly graph serialization or additional encoding and alignment procedures.
GRIP fine-tunes LLM parameters to internalize graph knowledge and stores it in LoRA modules.
The authors report improved performance for graphs beyond the context window and lower inference cost for small graphs.
